# Zilkworm Documentation: full corpus

---
# Overview

Source: https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/

_Zilkworm runs stateless Ethereum block execution in RISC-V zkVM guests and ships provers for Airbender and SP1 Hypercube._

# Zilkworm

Zilkworm is a stateless Ethereum block execution engine in C++, compiled to RISC-V guests for zkVMs.
Each proof covers one block: it shows the guest ran the block from its witness and committed the result.
Ethproofs operators run it to prove mainnet blocks, researchers use it to estimate proving cost, and contributors build and test it.

The code is on [GitHub](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm), and release assets are on the [releases page](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/releases).

---
# Choosing a prover

Source: https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/provers/choosing-a-prover

_Compare the Airbender and Hypercube provers, the HashState guest and the ZisK backend by zkVM, artifacts, hardware and status._

# Choosing a prover

Zilkworm compiles one C++ block execution engine into a RISC-V guest for each zkVM. The table compares them at release v0.1.0-alpha.7.

| Prover | zkVM | ISA | What ships | Inputs | Host check | Hardware | Status | Ethproofs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Airbender](./airbender-prover.md) | Airbender v3 | `rv32im_zicsr` | Image `ghcr.io/erigontech/zilkworm-airbender`; guest `.bin`, `.text` and `.vk` | MFBD, EJSN | Fails on a block hash mismatch | 32 GB VRAM per GPU, CUDA 13.1 driver | Live | One live cluster |
| [Hypercube](./hypercube-prover.md), MFBD guest | SP1 Hypercube v6.9.0 | `rv64im` | Binary `z6m_prover_hypercube`; guest `.elf` and `.vk` | MFBD, EJSN | Logs public values only | Not stated in the repo | Shipped | No live cluster |
| [HashState guest](../testing/ere-validation.md), ERE | SP1 v6.9.0 | `rv64im` | `stateless-validator-zilkworm-sp1-v6.9.0.elf` and `.vk` | SSZ `statelessInputBytes`, EJSN | ere-hosts compares the output | Not stated in the repo | Shipped | No |
| [ZisK](./zisk-prover.md) | ZisK v1.3.1-alpha | `rv64im_zicsr_zba_zbb_zbs_zbkb` | Nothing yet, draft PR #86 | MFBD, EJSN | Verifies each proof before saving | CUDA 12.9, about 25 GB RAM | In progress | No |

Pick Airbender to post proofs to Ethproofs today. Its cluster "Zilkworm Airbender v3 2x5090 on-prem" is the only live Zilkworm cluster on [ethproofs.org/provers](https://ethproofs.org/provers), checked 2026-10-26. Its Docker image runs the whole service from environment variables.

Pick Hypercube to execute blocks and measure SP1 cycles, or to build on the MFBD guest. Its `execute` subcommand runs on the CPU and prints cycles and prover gas. Its service can post to Ethproofs, but no Zilkworm Hypercube cluster posts today.

The HashState guest is for ERE validation and cost estimates, not for operators. ere-hosts feeds it each fixture's `statelessInputBytes` and compares its 43-byte output with the expected one.

## Further reading

- [Ethproofs posting](./ethproofs-posting.md)
- [Execution pipeline](../inside-the-guest/execution-pipeline.md)
- [Releases and assets](../reference/releases-and-assets.md)
- [ERE validation](../testing/ere-validation.md)
- [`docs/architecture.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/architecture.md)

# Airbender prover

Source: https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/provers/airbender-prover

_Run the Airbender GPU prover from its Docker image to follow the chain, prove blocks and post them to Ethproofs._

# Airbender prover

The Airbender prover runs Zilkworm on ZKsync Airbender v3. It ships as a Docker image with the host, the guest and the CUDA runtime. Airbender is the zkVM behind the only live Zilkworm cluster on Ethproofs.

## Shipped artifacts

Release v0.1.0-alpha.7 publishes the image `ghcr.io/erigontech/zilkworm-airbender:v0.1.0-alpha.7`. A push to `main` that changes the image inputs also tags it with its commit sha and with `:main`. Pulling needs no credentials.

The image holds four things:

- `/usr/local/bin/z6m_prover_airbender`: the host, with the witness converter linked in.
- `/opt/z6m/z6m_guest.bin` and `.text`: the guest.
- `/opt/z6m/fsv/`: the three recursion verifier programs, each as a `.bin` and a `.text` file.
- `/usr/local/bin/airbender-entrypoint`: the entrypoint.

The release also attaches the guest and its key:

- `z6m_guest_airbender.bin` and `z6m_guest_airbender.text`: the guest, copied out of the image.
- `z6m_guest_airbender.vk`: its `EVKEY001` v2 verification key. Register it with Ethproofs for a cluster that runs this release.

The release notes give the image digest and the key's sha256.

The guest targets `rv32im_zicsr` with the `ilp32` ABI. It reads MFBD witness bundles and EEST JSON fixtures wrapped as EJSN. [Witness formats](../inside-the-guest/witness-formats.md) describes both.

## Hardware

- NVIDIA GPUs with at least 32 GB of VRAM each. All GPUs the container sees prove the same block together.
- About 24 GB of pinned host RAM per GPU, plus a few GB for the service.
- An NVIDIA driver for CUDA 13.1 or newer, and the NVIDIA Container Toolkit.
- A GPU of compute capability 8.0, 8.9, 9.0 or 12.0. B200 is 10.0 and is not supported.
- About 96 GB of RAM for the CPU backend of `prove`, if you use it.
- Disk for the data directory: a few MB per fetched block and about 1 MB per proof.

## Run it

### Proving service

```bash
export RPC_URL=http://<execution-client>:8545
docker run -d --name zilkworm-airbender --gpus all --restart unless-stopped \
  -v /srv/zilkworm-airbender:/data \
  -e RPC_URL -e PROVE_EVERY=100 \
  ghcr.io/erigontech/zilkworm-airbender:v0.1.0-alpha.7
```

The node behind `RPC_URL` must serve `debug_executionWitness`. With no arguments, the entrypoint runs the service and starts it again 30 s after any exit. On first start it computes the verification key on the CPU, which takes about two minutes. The service then follows the chain tip and proves every block whose number is a multiple of `PROVE_EVERY`.

Outputs land in `/srv/zilkworm-airbender`:

- `proofs/<N>/proof.bin`: one proof per proved block.
- `provingLogs.log`: one line per proved, skipped or failed block.
- `blocks/<N>/flatWitnessBundle<N>.mfbd`: each fetched bundle.
- `vk-<revision>-<id>/vk.bin`: the verification key the entrypoint computed.

Service logs go to stdout. Read them with `docker logs -f zilkworm-airbender`.

The entrypoint reads these variables:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `RPC_URL` | JSON-RPC endpoint that serves `debug_executionWitness`; required |
| `WS_URL` | WebSocket endpoint for `newHeads`; without it the service polls |
| `PROVE_EVERY` | Prove blocks whose number is a multiple of this; default 100 |
| `EXECUTE_EVERY` | Execute without proving every N-th block; default none |
| `START_BLOCK` | First block; default the chain tip |
| `FETCH_TIMEOUT` | Seconds one fetch attempt may take; default 60 |
| `MAX_LAG` | Blocks the service may fall behind the tip before it skips ahead; default 10, 0 never skips |
| `DATA_DIR` | Key, blocks, logs and proofs; default `/data` |
| `ETHPROOFS_ENDPOINT`, `ETHPROOFS_TOKEN`, `ETHPROOFS_CLUSTER_ID` | Post to Ethproofs when all three are set |
| `RESTART_DELAY` | Seconds before a restart; default 30 |
| `PROVER_EXTRA_ARGS` | Further prover options, split on spaces |

[Ethproofs posting](./ethproofs-posting.md) shows the service with the three Ethproofs variables set.

On hosts whose NVIDIA runtime uses CDI, `--gpus all` does not reach the GPUs. Use `--runtime=nvidia -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all` instead.

### One-block execution

With arguments, the entrypoint runs `z6m_prover_airbender` with them and adds the guest path. The image has no fetch command. Use a bundle the service fetched, or one from the `fetch` subcommand of the [Hypercube prover](./hypercube-prover.md).

```bash
N=$(ls /srv/zilkworm-airbender/blocks | sort -n | tail -1)
docker run --rm -v /srv/zilkworm-airbender/blocks/$N:/in:ro \
  ghcr.io/erigontech/zilkworm-airbender:v0.1.0-alpha.7 \
  execute --file-name /in/flatWitnessBundle$N.mfbd
```

`execute` runs the guest on the simulator, without a GPU. It prints an `Executed block` line with gas used and cycles, then the block hash the guest committed. The result goes to stdout only.

### One-block proof

```bash
N=$(ls /srv/zilkworm-airbender/blocks | sort -n | tail -1)
mkdir -p out
docker run --rm --gpus all \
  -v /srv/zilkworm-airbender/blocks/$N:/in:ro -v "$PWD/out:/out" \
  ghcr.io/erigontech/zilkworm-airbender:v0.1.0-alpha.7 \
  prove --file-name /in/flatWitnessBundle$N.mfbd --output-dir /out
```

The proof lands in `out/proof.bin`. `prove` runs the simulator first. If the guest rejects the block, `prove` stops with an error and writes no proof.

### Proof verification

```bash
N=$(ls /srv/zilkworm-airbender/blocks | sort -n | tail -1)
curl -LO https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.7/z6m_guest_airbender.vk
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/w" -v /srv/zilkworm-airbender/blocks/$N:/in:ro \
  ghcr.io/erigontech/zilkworm-airbender:v0.1.0-alpha.7 \
  verify --proof /w/out/proof.bin --vk /w/z6m_guest_airbender.vk \
  --file-name /in/flatWitnessBundle$N.mfbd
```

`verify` runs on the CPU. Pass `--block-hash` instead of `--file-name` when the input is not at hand.

## Inputs and outputs

The service follows the chain head by polling `eth_blockNumber`, or through `newHeads` when `WS_URL` is set. For each block it calls `eth_getBlockByNumber`, `debug_getRawBlock` and `debug_executionWitness`. It tries a block up to five times, each within `FETCH_TIMEOUT`, and then skips it. It converts the response to an MFBD bundle in process and writes `<data-dir>/blocks/<N>/flatWitnessBundle<N>.mfbd`.

The guest reads its input through the CSR oracle at `0x7C0`, as [Precompiles and syscalls](../inside-the-guest/precompiles-and-syscalls.md) describes. It commits 32 bytes of public values: the hash of the last block it validated. The bytes sit as little-endian words in registers `a0` to `a7`. An EJSN run commits zero. A failed run ends at `finish_error` and commits nothing. [Proof guarantees](../inside-the-guest/proof-guarantees.md) gives the full layout.

`proof.bin` is a gzipped `EPROOF01` v2 envelope, the format Ethproofs takes. The key is an `EVKEY001` v2 file.

## Host checks

The host derives the expected public output from the input alone. It reads the MFBD bundle and takes the hash of the last block not flagged invalid. `execute`, `prove`, `verify`, `--test-service` and `--service` all fail when the guest commits any other value.

The service runs each block on the simulator before it proves it. It proves only a run that reaches the guest's exit point within the prover's cycle limit. That run and the proof must both commit the expected hash. Otherwise the block is logged as `SKIPPED` in `provingLogs.log`. A prover panic logs the block as `FAILED`. The service then rebuilds the prover and moves on.

## Known limits

- The prover takes at most 1,073,741,822 cycles per block. A heavier block is skipped.
- The `cpu` backend of `prove` is very slow and needs the RAM listed under Hardware.
- The image has no kernels for B200 GPUs.
- `prover/prover_airbender/eest-known-failures.txt` lists 25 EEST fixtures the guest does not finish. They hit resource limits; they are not wrong results.
- A restarted service starts at the chain tip. Blocks between a crash and the restart are not proved.
- Reth's witness can miss an account that the block deletes. The guest recovers it from its trie path when the witness has that path. Otherwise the preflight fails and the block is skipped.
- Reth serves no witness for a block more than about 12 blocks behind its tip. An old `START_BLOCK` gets no witnesses from reth.
- The prover's pinned host memory is not configurable.

## Measured

At v0.1.0-alpha.5, the guest proved 200 consecutive mainnet blocks at a 3.4 s median on 2x RTX 5090. Figures for each release are on [Releases and assets](../reference/releases-and-assets.md).

- [Ethproofs posting](./ethproofs-posting.md)

# Hypercube prover

Source: https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/provers/hypercube-prover

_Run the SP1 Hypercube prover binary to execute blocks with the MFBD guest or prove them on a GPU._

# Hypercube prover

The Hypercube prover runs Zilkworm on SP1 Hypercube v6.9.0. It ships as one Linux binary with the guest built in. It can execute blocks, prove them and post to Ethproofs. No Zilkworm Hypercube cluster posts to Ethproofs today.

## Shipped artifacts

Release v0.1.0-alpha.7 attaches three Hypercube files:

- `z6m_prover_hypercube`: the host for x86_64 Linux. It names itself `z6m_prover` and embeds the guest below.
- `z6m_guest_hypercube_mfbd.elf`: the DirectState guest, `rv64im` with the `lp64` ABI.
- `z6m_guest_hypercube_mfbd.vk`: its 32-byte SP1 program verification key.

The host builds on the `erigon/patches-v6.9.0` branch of `erigontech/sp1`. Keys published for alpha.6 do not verify alpha.7 proofs.

The guest reads MFBD witness bundles. With `--is-test`, the host wraps an EEST JSON fixture as EJSN. Raw SSZ input makes this guest return an error; the [HashState guest](../testing/ere-validation.md) takes that format. [Witness formats](../inside-the-guest/witness-formats.md) describes all three.

## Hardware

The repo states no VRAM or RAM figure for SP1 proving.

`execute` runs on the CPU. GPU proving needs an NVIDIA GPU and SP1's `sp1-gpu-server`. No release asset carries `sp1-gpu-server`. The root `Dockerfile` builds it from `erigontech/sp1` with `CUDA_ARCHS=89` by default.

## Run it

Download the binary and point it at a node:

```bash
curl -LO https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.7/z6m_prover_hypercube
chmod +x z6m_prover_hypercube
export RPC_URL=http://<execution-client>:8545
```

The node must serve `debug_getRawBlock` and `debug_executionWitness`.

### Proving service

```bash
SP1_PROVER=cuda ./z6m_prover_hypercube --service \
  --rpc-url "$RPC_URL" --data-dir data --prove-every 100
```

The service starts at the chain head plus one and runs until stopped. It fetches and proves every block whose number is a multiple of 100. It skips other blocks without fetching them. Without `SP1_PROVER=cuda`, it proves on the CPU.

Outputs land in `data/`:

- `blocks/<N>/flatWitnessBundle<N>.mfbd`: each fetched bundle.
- `<N>/proof<N>.bin`: each proof, outside `blocks/`.
- `provingLogs.log`: one line per proved or failed block.
- `executionLogs.log`: one line per executed block.

`--execute-every N` adds execution runs for blocks that are not proved. `--end-block` stops the service after that block. [Ethproofs posting](./ethproofs-posting.md) adds the three Ethproofs flags.

### One-block execution

```bash
./z6m_prover_hypercube fetch --rpc-url "$RPC_URL" --data-dir data
N=$(ls data/blocks | sort -n | tail -1)
./z6m_prover_hypercube execute --block-number $N --data-dir data
```

`fetch` without `--block-number` takes the chain head. It writes `data/blocks/<N>/flatWitnessBundle<N>.mfbd`. Add `--geth` to `fetch` for a Geth node.

`execute` runs the guest in the SP1 executor on the CPU. It prints `Executed block <N>` with gas used, cycles, prover gas and syscall count. It also appends a line to `data/executionLogs.log`.

### One-block proof

:::warning
The `prove` subcommand writes no proof file. To prove one block, run the service bounded to that block, as below. [Known limits](#known-limits) explains why.
:::

```bash
N=$(ls data/blocks | sort -n | tail -1)
SP1_PROVER=cuda ./z6m_prover_hypercube --service --rpc-url "$RPC_URL" --data-dir data \
  --start-block $N --end-block $N --prove-every 1
```

The service fetches the block again, so the node must still serve its witness. The proof lands in `data/<N>/proof<N>.bin`. The service exits once the proof is written.

## Inputs and outputs

The service follows the chain head with `eth_blockNumber`. For each block it calls `eth_getBlockByNumber`, `debug_getRawBlock` and `debug_executionWitness`. It reads the witness in the reth shape; only `fetch --geth` reads the Geth shape. It converts the response to an MFBD bundle in process. `fetch` reuses a bundle already on disk, and the service always rebuilds it. `--save-all-responses` also writes `block<N>.json`, `blockRlp<N>.json` and `executionWitness<N>.json`.

The host passes the bundle unchanged on SP1 stdin. The guest commits 112 bytes of public values: `gas_used`, the pre-state root, the post-state root, the block hash and the chain id. [Proof guarantees](../inside-the-guest/proof-guarantees.md) gives the byte layout.

A proof file holds a bincode-encoded `SP1ProofWithPublicValues`. `--proof-type` picks `core`, `compressed`, `groth16` or `plonk`. The default is `compressed`, and unknown values fall back to it. The service proves one block at a time, with a 30-minute timeout per proof.

## Host checks

The service parses the 112-byte public values of each proof and logs them. It does not compare them with the input or the chain. `execute` treats a `gas_used` of 0 as a failure and exits 1. The guest's own checks are on [Proof guarantees](../inside-the-guest/proof-guarantees.md).

## Known limits

At v0.1.0-alpha.7:

- `prove` discards the proof and writes no file.
- `prove` exits 0 when setup fails, after printing `ERROR` and the cause.
- `prove` always uses CUDA, whatever `SP1_PROVER` says.
- `verify` is a no-op.
- `setup` is a no-op.
- The service logs the 112-byte public values and does not compare them with the input.
- `--post-every`, `--pk-path` and `--proof-path` are accepted and unused.
- The Docker image `somnergy/z6m_prover` is built by hand from the root `Dockerfile`. No workflow publishes it.

## Measured

At v0.1.0-alpha.7, no proving time is published. Guest cycle counts are on [Releases and assets](../reference/releases-and-assets.md).

## Further reading

- [Ethproofs posting](./ethproofs-posting.md)
- [CLI reference](../reference/cli-reference.md)
- [Execution spec tests](../testing/execution-spec-tests.md)
- [`prover/prover_hypercube/src/main.rs`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/prover/prover_hypercube/src/main.rs)
- [`docs/architecture.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/architecture.md)

# ZisK prover

Source: https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/provers/zisk-prover

_The ZisK backend lives in draft PR #86, runs execute-only in CI and has had one GPU proving run._

# ZisK prover

ZisK support lives in [PR #86](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/pull/86), a draft based on alpha.6. It is not on `main`, and no release ships it. It runs Zilkworm on ZisK v1.3.1-alpha. Every command below runs from a checkout of the PR branch, `som/zisk-impl`.

## Shipped artifacts

No release carries ZisK files. The branch adds:

- `prover/guest_zisk/`: the guest, built for `rv64im_zicsr_zba_zbb_zbs_zbkb`.
- `prover/prover_zisk/`: the host `z6m_prover_zisk`, on `zisk-sdk` 1.3.1-alpha.
- `zisk-eest.yml` and `zisk-benchmark.yml`: two CI workflows on the image `ghcr.io/erigontech/zilkworm-ci-zisk`.

The host has the same commands and log format as `z6m_prover`: `setup`, `fetch`, `execute`, `prove`, `verify`, `--test-service` and `--service`. It adds `--executor`, `--elf`, `--proving-key` and `--remote`. `--executor` picks `emulator`, the default, or `assembly` or `ziskemu`.

The guest reads MFBD witness bundles. With `--is-test`, the host wraps an EEST JSON fixture as EJSN. The ZisK EEST job runs MFBD files that `make eest-mfbd-build` converts.

## Hardware

- An NVIDIA driver 525.60.13 or newer.
- CUDA Toolkit 12.9 or newer, installed under `/usr/local/cuda`.
- About 25 GB of RAM per prover process, as ZisK's docs state.
- At least 64 GB of RAM for the `assembly` executor, and at least 32 GB for the Rust emulator.
- An unlimited memlock limit, for the `assembly` executor only.
- About 21 GB of disk for the proving key once it is set up.
- Ubuntu 22.04 or newer. The reference machine runs Ubuntu 25.10.

ZisK documents no VRAM figure. The one GPU run used a 32 GB card and filled it on every block.

## Run it

No service command has run against a live node yet. The steps below build the backend, execute a block and prove it.

### Toolchain and ZisK

Install xPack `riscv-none-elf-gcc` 15.2.0-1.1 and no other version. The Makefile puts the first xPack version it finds on `PATH`, so an older one next to it wins silently.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm.git && cd zilkworm
git checkout som/zisk-impl
git submodule update --init --recursive
sudo npm install --global xpm@latest
xpm install @xpack-dev-tools/riscv-none-elf-gcc@15.2.0-1.1 --global
mkdir -p ~/.zisk/bin
curl -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygonHermez/zisk/v1.3.1-alpha/ziskup/ziskup -o ~/.zisk/bin/ziskup
chmod +x ~/.zisk/bin/ziskup
mkdir -p temp/runtime && cd temp/runtime
~/.zisk/bin/ziskup --version 1.3.1-alpha --gpu --provingkey
cd - && source ~/.bashrc
cargo-zisk-dev check-setup --proving-key ~/.zisk/provingKey --gpu
```

`ziskup` installs ZisK into `~/.zisk` and the proving key into `~/.zisk/provingKey`. It downloads the key tarball into the current directory, hence `temp/runtime`. Always pass `--version`. Without it, `ziskup` installs the latest release, whose key and binaries do not match the host.

`ziskup` runs `check-setup` with `-a`, which skips the recursive setups. The last command checks them. The full package list and the fixes for Ubuntu 25.10 are in `docs/zisk-docs.md` on the branch.

### Guest and host build

```bash
make z6m_guest_zisk
(cd prover/prover_zisk && cargo build --release --no-default-features --features gpu)
```

The guest lands in `prover/guest_zisk/build/z6m_guest.elf`. The GPU host lands in `prover/prover_zisk/target/release/z6m_prover_zisk`. `make z6m_prover_zisk` writes a CPU-only host to the same path and replaces the GPU one.

### Block execution

Get the 200-block mainnet corpus and convert it to MFBD:

```bash
curl -L -o temp/200_benchmark_blocks.tar.gz \
  https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm-testdata/releases/download/benchmark-200-spread/200_benchmark_blocks.tar.gz
tar xzf temp/200_benchmark_blocks.tar.gz -C temp && rm temp/200_benchmark_blocks.tar.gz
make sp1-benchmark-corpus
```

The bundles land in `temp/200_benchmark_blocks_mfbd_v2/<N>/flatWitnessBundle<N>.mfbd`. Execute one block under `ziskemu`:

```bash
P=prover/prover_zisk/target/release/z6m_prover_zisk
$P --executor ziskemu execute \
  --file-name temp/200_benchmark_blocks_mfbd_v2/24545295/flatWitnessBundle24545295.mfbd
```

`execute` needs no proving key. It prints an `Executed block` line and a `Public Values:` line to stdout. With `--file-name`, it prints the block number as 0. `make zisk-emu-check` runs all 200 blocks and compares their public values with native `state_transition`.

### Block proof

Keep temporary files on disk. `/tmp` is often in RAM, and the ZisK SDK writes temporary files there.

```bash
export TMPDIR=$PWD/temp/runtime/tmp && mkdir -p "$TMPDIR" temp/proofs
P=prover/prover_zisk/target/release/z6m_prover_zisk
$P setup
$P prove --file-name temp/200_benchmark_blocks_mfbd_v2/24545295/flatWitnessBundle24545295.mfbd \
  --proof-path temp/proofs/24545295.bin
$P verify --proof-path temp/proofs/24545295.bin
```

The proof lands in `temp/proofs/24545295.bin`. `prove` also appends a line to `temp/provingLogs.log`. Run `setup` once per guest ELF, because `verify` needs the program key it caches.

Each `prove` process loads the proving key again. To prove many blocks, run them in one process:

```bash
mkdir -p temp/zisk_gpu_run && ln -sfn ../200_benchmark_blocks_mfbd_v2 temp/zisk_gpu_run/blocks
$P --test-service --data-dir temp/zisk_gpu_run \
  --start-block 24491136 --end-block 24640322 --prove-every 1
```

Proofs land in `temp/zisk_gpu_run/<N>/proof<N>.bin`, with one log line each in `temp/zisk_gpu_run/provingLogs.log`.

## Inputs and outputs

The host reads MFBD bundles by path, or from `<data-dir>/blocks/<N>/` in `--test-service` mode. The guest commits 112 bytes of public values, the same layout as the Hypercube guest. They sit in ZisK output slots 0 to 27. [Proof guarantees](../inside-the-guest/proof-guarantees.md) gives the layout.

`prove` writes the proof to `--proof-path`. The default proof type is `compressed`, which ZisK calls VadcopFinal.

## Host checks

`prove` verifies each new proof before it saves it. `verify` checks a proof against the program key from the setup cache. `tools/scripts/zisk_execute.py` and `make zisk-emu-check` compare the public values with native `state_transition`.

Inside the guest, every free-input hint from a ZisK precompile is checked. A bad inverse, square root or division hint halts the guest, so no proof exists. A bad GLV hint falls back to plain code.

## Known limits

- PR #86 is a draft based on alpha.6. It lacks the changes merged to `main` after alpha.6.
- No release ships ZisK files.
- CI is execute-only. Both ZisK workflows run the guest under `ziskemu`, with no proving key, no GPU and no proofs.
- One GPU run so far, on one RTX 5090 with `compressed` proofs.
- Not tested yet: the `minimal` and `plonk` proof types, more than one GPU, the `assembly` executor, `--remote`, and `--service` against a live node.
- On EEST at tests@v21.0.1, 12,253 of 12,266 fixtures pass and 10 are skipped over the 20 MB size cap. Three fail.
- Two of those failures need more than ZisK's fixed 512 MiB of RAM. The third, `tx_invalid_first_in_block`, also failed on SP1 at alpha.6. PR #141 on `main` fixes it, and the branch lacks that fix.
- Ethproofs posting for ZisK is deferred.
- `--executor ziskemu` is execute-only. `prove` with it exits 1.
- `ziskemu` exits 0 when the guest halts with an error. Check stderr for `finished with error`.
- The prover fills the VRAM of a 32 GB card. The host does not yet expose `max_streams` or `minimal_memory` for smaller cards.

## Measured

PR #86 reports one GPU run, on 2026-10-08. One RTX 5090 proved 200 of 200 corpus blocks at a median proving time of 31.5 s. ZisK has no release, so [Releases and assets](../reference/releases-and-assets.md) lists no ZisK figures.

## Further reading

- [Choosing a prover](./choosing-a-prover.md)
- [Hypercube prover](./hypercube-prover.md)
- [Execution spec tests](../testing/execution-spec-tests.md)
- [PR #86](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/pull/86)
- [`docs/zisk-docs.md` on `som/zisk-impl`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/som/zisk-impl/docs/zisk-docs.md)

# Ethproofs posting

Source: https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/provers/ethproofs-posting

_The Airbender and Hypercube services report each proved block to Ethproofs once an endpoint, a token and a cluster id are set._

# Ethproofs posting

[Ethproofs](https://ethproofs.org) collects proofs of Ethereum blocks from registered proving clusters. The Airbender and Hypercube services can report to it. The ZisK backend cannot yet.

## Live clusters

One Zilkworm cluster posts today: "Zilkworm Airbender v3 2x5090 on-prem". It was the only one on [ethproofs.org/provers](https://ethproofs.org/provers) when checked on 2026-10-26. The Hypercube service has the same posting code, but no Zilkworm Hypercube cluster posts.

## Three settings

Posting needs all three of these:

- `--ethproofs-endpoint`: the API base URL. The service appends paths such as `/proofs/queued` to it.
- `--ethproofs-token`: the API token, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- `--ethproofs-cluster-id`: the numeric cluster id.

With any of them unset, the service still proves but posts nothing. Only `--service` mode posts. The `prove` subcommands of both binaries never post. Both binaries accept `--post-every`, and neither uses it.

The repo documents no production endpoint. Its examples in `docs/airbender-docker-service.md` and `prover/prover_airbender/README.md` use the staging API, `https://staging--ethproofs.netlify.app/api/v0`. Replace `<endpoint>` below with the URL Ethproofs gives your cluster.

Each binary takes the settings in its own way:

- `z6m_prover_hypercube` reads the three flags only.
- `z6m_prover_airbender` reads the flags or the variables `ETHPROOFS_ENDPOINT`, `ETHPROOFS_TOKEN` and `ETHPROOFS_CLUSTER_ID`.
- The Airbender image reads the three variables. If one is missing, its entrypoint unsets all three and logs that nothing is posted.

## Posting lifecycle

For each block it proves, the service sends three POST requests:

1. `/proofs/queued` when the service picks the block, before it waits for the prover.
2. `/proofs/proving` when proving starts.
3. `/proofs/proved` after a successful proof.

`queued` and `proving` carry `block_number` and `cluster_id`. `proved` carries five fields:

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| `block_number` | The block number |
| `cluster_id` | The cluster id |
| `proving_time` | Proving time in milliseconds, measured by the host |
| `proving_cycles` | The guest's cycle count |
| `proof` | The proof file, base64-encoded |

The proof file is `proof.bin` for Airbender and `proof<N>.bin` for Hypercube. For Airbender, `proving_time` leaves out fetching, witness conversion and the preflight. Airbender posts a proof only after the preflight and the proof both commit the expected block hash.

Each request has a 60 s timeout. `queued` and `proving` are sent once. A `proved` post that gets a 429, a 5xx or no answer is tried up to four times in all:

- After a 429, the service waits as long as the body's `retryAfter` or the `Retry-After` header asks. The default is 30 s.
- After a 5xx or no answer, it waits 10 s.
- No wait is longer than 120 s.
- A 409 on a retry means an earlier attempt landed, and the service stops.

Other errors are logged and not retried. Posts run in the background and never hold up proving. A failed post leaves the proof on disk.

## Cluster and verification key

Ethproofs checks a cluster's proofs against the key registered for it. A cluster that runs the Airbender image registers `z6m_guest_airbender.vk` from the same release:

```bash
curl -LO https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.7/z6m_guest_airbender.vk
sha256sum z6m_guest_airbender.vk
```

The alpha.7 release notes give its sha256 as `ffcdff786029d7f9621ad8c23ece641de9d72c38ecb1097d1d4b5e3e583c1de5`. A cluster that moves to a new release image needs that release's key. On first start, the image's entrypoint also computes a key and logs its sha256.

The repo documents no Ethproofs key upload for Hypercube proofs.

## Command examples

### Airbender image

```bash
export RPC_URL=http://<execution-client>:8545
export ETHPROOFS_ENDPOINT=<endpoint>
export ETHPROOFS_TOKEN=<api-token>
export ETHPROOFS_CLUSTER_ID=<cluster-id>
docker run -d --name zilkworm-airbender --gpus all --restart unless-stopped \
  -v /srv/zilkworm-airbender:/data \
  -e RPC_URL -e PROVE_EVERY=100 \
  -e ETHPROOFS_ENDPOINT -e ETHPROOFS_TOKEN -e ETHPROOFS_CLUSTER_ID \
  ghcr.io/erigontech/zilkworm-airbender:v0.1.0-alpha.7
```

The entrypoint logs `posting to Ethproofs at` with the endpoint and cluster id. Proofs land in `/srv/zilkworm-airbender/proofs/<N>/proof.bin`. [Airbender prover](./airbender-prover.md) covers the rest of the service.

### Hypercube binary

```bash
export RPC_URL=http://<execution-client>:8545
export ETHPROOFS_ENDPOINT=<endpoint>
export ETHPROOFS_TOKEN=<api-token>
export ETHPROOFS_CLUSTER_ID=<cluster-id>
SP1_PROVER=cuda ./z6m_prover_hypercube --service \
  --rpc-url "$RPC_URL" --data-dir data --prove-every 100 \
  --ethproofs-endpoint "$ETHPROOFS_ENDPOINT" \
  --ethproofs-token "$ETHPROOFS_TOKEN" \
  --ethproofs-cluster-id "$ETHPROOFS_CLUSTER_ID"
```

Proofs land in `data/<N>/proof<N>.bin`. [Hypercube prover](./hypercube-prover.md) covers the rest of the service.

## Further reading

- [Airbender prover](./airbender-prover.md)
- [Hypercube prover](./hypercube-prover.md)
- [Releases and assets](../reference/releases-and-assets.md)
- [`prover/common/src/ethproofs_client.rs`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/prover/common/src/ethproofs_client.rs)
- [`docs/airbender-docker-service.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/airbender-docker-service.md)

# Execution pipeline

Source: https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/inside-the-guest/execution-pipeline

_A host feeds a block and its witness to a RISC-V guest, the guest commits public values, and the proof ties them to one guest ELF._

# Execution pipeline

Zilkworm is a C++ program that runs Ethereum blocks without a state database. It is compiled to RISC-V once per zkVM. The zkVM runs that guest program and proves the run.

## Four steps from block to proof

1. Witness in. The host fetches a block and its execution witness from a node. It packs them into one input buffer for the guest. On the ERE path, the harness passes a fixture's `statelessInputBytes` unchanged instead.
2. Guest runs. The zkVM runs the guest on that input. The guest anchors the pre-state to the parent header's state root. It runs every transaction, then checks the header's state root and gas used against the run.
3. Public values out. The guest commits a short, fixed record of the result. Depending on the guest, it holds state roots, the block hash, gas used or a validation flag.
4. Proof. The zkVM proves the run. The proof ties the public values to one guest ELF through that ELF's verifying key.

[Witness formats](./witness-formats.md) describes the inputs. [Proof guarantees](./proof-guarantees.md) lists each guest's public values and what a proof leaves out.

## Host and guest

Each zkVM integration has two programs.

- The host is Rust, under `prover/prover_*`. It runs natively. It fetches blocks over JSON-RPC, builds the input and drives the zkVM. In service mode it can also post proofs to Ethproofs.
- The guest is a bare-metal RISC-V program, under `prover/guest_*`. It reads the input, calls the C++ core and commits the public values. No operating system runs underneath it.

The core, `zilk_core`, is one C++23 library. It started as a fork of Silkworm's core: execution, state, protocol rules, trie, RLP and types. It builds natively for development and tests. For each zkVM it is cross-compiled into that zkVM's guest with the xPack `riscv-none-elf-gcc` toolchain.

The Hypercube host embeds its guest ELF at compile time. `prover/prover_hypercube/build.rs` points `include_elf!` at the ELF that `make z6m_guest` builds. The Airbender host loads its guest image from the path in `--guest-bin`. Both hosts also link C++ code directly. Their fetcher converts a node's witness to MFBD through the `prover/witness_ffi` bridge.

## Transaction execution with evmone

Zilkworm embeds evmone to execute transactions. Its fork, ZVM1, lives in `third_party/evmone`. The Zilkworm core handles blocks, the witness, state and the trie. It calls evmone once per transaction. evmone is one component of the guest, not the guest itself.

The zkVM-specific acceleration for hashing and curve math sits mostly in evmone's precompile code. [Precompiles and syscalls](./precompiles-and-syscalls.md) lists it per zkVM.

## Guest targets

Each zkVM gets its own guest build, and the zkVM sets the ISA.

| Guest | Source and build | ISA (`-march`) | Inputs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hypercube MFBD guest, SP1 | `prover/guest_hypercube`, `make z6m_guest` | `rv64im` | MFBD, EJSN |
| HashState guest, SP1 | `prover/guest_hypercube`, `make z6m_guest_slib` | `rv64im` | `statelessInputBytes`, EJSN |
| Airbender guest | `prover/guest_airbender`, `make z6m_guest_airbender` | `rv32im_zicsr` | MFBD, EJSN |
| ZisK guest, draft PR #86 | `prover/guest_zisk`, `make z6m_guest_zisk` | `rv64im_zicsr_zba_zbb_zbs_zbkb` | MFBD, EJSN |

Airbender's proving machine has only the unsigned multiply and divide instructions. Its guest therefore avoids `mulh`, `mulhsu`, `div` and `rem`. A post-link check, `prover/guest_airbender/cmake/check_unsigned_muldiv.cmake`, guards this in the build.

The ZisK guest exists only on [PR #86](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/pull/86), a draft based on alpha.6. No release ships it.

## DirectState and HashState

DirectState is the default state backend. It reads an MFBD bundle in place: accounts, storage, code and trie nodes sit in flat sections the guest does not decode. The run takes the pre-state root from the parent header that the first block names. When the block ends, the trie fold binds each touched key's pre-value to that root and recomputes the post-state root. That root must match the header. The Hypercube MFBD guest, the Airbender and ZisK guests and the native runner all use DirectState.

HashState takes the EIP-8025 `statelessInputBytes` unchanged. It walks each trie path from the parent state root at the moment of the read, so every read is checked against that root. A read the witness cannot confirm, as a value or as a proven absence, rejects the block. After the run, the guest folds the block's writes over the parent root and accepts only on a matching root. The backend is fixed at compile time with `-DZ6M_HASH_STATE=ON`, with no runtime switch. The HashState build is the ERE guest, released as `stateless-validator-zilkworm-sp1-<SP1 version>.elf`.

## Further reading

- [Witness formats](./witness-formats.md)
- [Proof guarantees](./proof-guarantees.md)
- [Precompiles and syscalls](./precompiles-and-syscalls.md)
- [Choosing a prover](../provers/choosing-a-prover.md)
- [`docs/hashstate.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/hashstate.md): the HashState backend in depth

# Witness formats

Source: https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/inside-the-guest/witness-formats

_Guests read MFBD bundles, raw SSZ statelessInputBytes or EJSN-wrapped test fixtures, and each format has its own producers._

# Witness formats

A stateless run needs the block and the part of the state it touches. The host hands the guest one byte buffer that holds all of it. The guest reads the first bytes of that buffer to pick a path.

## MFBD bundles

An MFBD file is a 16-byte envelope followed by one or more flat bundles. The envelope is `<u32 magic><u32 version><u64 count>`, with magic `MFBD` (`0x4442464D`) and version 1. Each bundle starts with a 56-byte header, magic `FBND` (`0x444E4246`). The header points at six sections. They hold the genesis block, the blocks to run, the ancestor headers, the pre-state, the trie nodes and the network name. The guest reads each section where it lies instead of decoding it.

The bundle version is `kFlatBundleVersion` in `zilk_core/core/types_zz/flat_bundle.hpp`, now 14. `load_flat_bundle` rejects any other version, so a stale bundle fails at once.

## Raw statelessInputBytes

The HashState guest takes the EIP-8025 `statelessInputBytes`, the SSZ `StatelessInput` that tests-zkevm fixtures carry. It needs no wrapper. Its first two bytes are the schema id `0x1501`, big-endian, so the buffer starts `0x15 0x01`. No other input magic starts with `0x15`.

## EJSN test fixtures

EJSN wraps one EEST `blockchain_test` JSON fixture for a guest. The 8-byte header holds the magic `EJSN` (`0x4E534A45`) and version 1. The minified JSON follows. The hosts wrap a fixture this way when given `--is-test`, and the native runner wraps `.json` files itself. Under HashState, the guest reads each block's `statelessInputBytes` field from that JSON.

## Producers and consumers

| Format | Wire marker | Produced by | Consumed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| MFBD | `MFBD` v1 envelope, `FBND` v14 bundles | The host fetcher, through `prover/witness_ffi`; the CLIs `json_witness_to_flat_bundle`, `eest_to_flat_bundle` and `legacy_to_flat_bundle` | DirectState guests, native `state_transition`, the QEMU runner |
| `statelessInputBytes` | First bytes `0x15 0x01` | tests-zkevm fixtures from ethereum/execution-specs; ERE's `witness-generator-cli` | The HashState guest under ere-hosts; the native HashState tests, inside fixture JSON |
| EJSN | `EJSN` v1, 8-byte header | `z6m_prover --is-test`, `z6m_prover_airbender --is-test`, the native runner | Every guest, and native `state_transition` |
| Legacy unified RLP | None | The old fetcher | `legacy_to_flat_bundle` only |

The three CLIs live in `zilk_core/dev/cli`. `json_witness_to_flat_bundle` converts a node's `debug_executionWitness` JSON, and the host links the same converter. `eest_to_flat_bundle` converts EEST fixtures with `emit` or `bulk-convert`. `legacy_to_flat_bundle` converts old `unifiedBlockAndStateRlp<N>.bin` files.

## Formats each guest accepts

| Guest | Accepts | Any other input |
|---|---|---|
| Hypercube MFBD guest | MFBD, EJSN | Raw SSZ fails with "needs the HashState guest". Unknown magic fails the run. |
| HashState guest | Raw SSZ, EJSN | MFBD fails, since its path is compiled out. Anything else gives the all-zero result. |
| Airbender guest | MFBD, EJSN | Same as the Hypercube MFBD guest |
| ZisK guest, draft PR #86 | MFBD, EJSN | Same as the Hypercube MFBD guest |
| Native `state_transition` | `.mfbd` files, `.json` files wrapped as EJSN | Release builds lack HashState, so raw SSZ fails |

## Legacy unified RLP

`unifiedBlockAndStateRlp<N>.bin` files carry no magic, and no current guest reads them. They matter in two places. `legacy_to_flat_bundle` converts them to MFBD, and `make sp1-benchmark-corpus` runs that conversion. The Airbender host also falls back to that file name when a block has no `.mfbd` file, so convert old data first.

## Spec documents

The MFBD spec, `docs/mfbd_design_specs.md`, is normative. It says what a producer and a verifier must check. `docs/flat_witness_bundle.md` is the byte-layout reference. One diagram in the spec still says `FBND` v13; its section 4.2 and the code say 14.

## Further reading

- [Execution pipeline](./execution-pipeline.md)
- [Proof guarantees](./proof-guarantees.md)
- [`docs/mfbd_design_specs.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/mfbd_design_specs.md): the normative MFBD spec
- [`docs/flat_witness_bundle.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/flat_witness_bundle.md): the envelope and bundle byte layout
- [`docs/hashstate.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/hashstate.md): how HashState parses `statelessInputBytes`

# Precompiles and syscalls

Source: https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/inside-the-guest/precompiles-and-syscalls

_Each guest hands hashing and big-number math to its zkVM's circuits, through SP1 ecalls or Airbender and ZisK CSRs._

# Precompiles and syscalls

Hashing and curve math take many RISC-V instructions. A zkVM proves every instruction it runs, so plain code for these routines makes a long trace. Each zkVM offers dedicated circuits for them instead. The guest reaches a circuit through an `ecall` on SP1, or a CSR access on Airbender and ZisK. Each such call replaces a software routine the prover would otherwise trace cycle by cycle.

## SP1 ecalls

Both Hypercube guests declare their ecalls in `prover/guest_hypercube/src/include/sp1_syscalls.hpp`. Most wrappers are always inlined and compile to a single `ecall`. Most call sites sit in ZVM1, the evmone fork in `third_party/evmone`.

| Ecalls | Called from | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `keccak_permute` | `lib/evmone_precompiles/keccak.c` | Every Keccak-256 hash: KECCAK256, trie nodes, addresses |
| `sha256_extend`, `sha256_compress` | `lib/evmone_precompiles/sha256.cpp` | The SHA256 precompile, and the public-values digest |
| `secp256k1_add`, `secp256k1_double` | `lib/evmone_precompiles/secp256k1.cpp` | ECRECOVER and transaction sender recovery |
| `uint256_mulmod` | `lib/evmone/instructions.hpp`, `lib/evmone_precompiles/modexp.cpp` | ADDMOD, MULMOD and MODEXP |
| `bn254_fp_*mod`, `bn254_fp2_*mod` | `lib/evmone_precompiles/modarith.hpp`, `pairing/field_template.hpp` | Field math for ECADD, ECMUL and ECPAIRING |
| `bn254_add`, `bn254_double` | evmone's precompile dispatch, `test/state/precompiles.cpp` | Point math for ECADD and ECMUL |
| `bls12381_fp_*mod`, `bls12381_fp2_*mod` | `cmake/patch_blst_sp1.sh`, a build-time patch of blst | The BLS12-381 precompiles and KZG point evaluation |

The header also declares ecalls that nothing in the guest calls at the current ZVM1 pin. They are the secp256r1 and ed25519 point ecalls, `bls12381_add` and `bls12381_double`, `u256x2048_mul`, and the two `uint256_*_with_carry` calls.

The guest commits public values by writing to file descriptor 13, `SP1_FD_PUBLIC_VALUES`. The runtime in `prover/guest_hypercube/src/sp1_runtime.cpp` buffers those bytes. At halt it hashes them with SHA-256 and commits the digest.

## Airbender CSRs

The Airbender guest reaches its delegation circuits by writing to CSRs. `prover/guest_airbender/src/include/airbender_csr.hpp` names them.

| CSR | Name | Use in the guest |
|---|---|---|
| `0x7C0` | Non-determinism oracle | Reads the input words and writes log output |
| `0x7CA` | BigInt | 256-bit add, subtract, multiply, compare and copy |
| `0x7CC`, `0x7CD`, `0x7CE` | keccak_f1600: theta and rho, column parity, chi5 | One Keccak permutation per run of writes |
| `0x7C7` | Blake2s | Declared only; no guest code calls it |

The curve and scalar logic around these calls stays RISC-V code in ZVM1. The alpha.5 release notes map each precompile to a delegation:

| Precompile | Delegation | Code path |
|---|---|---|
| ECRECOVER, and every transaction's sender recovery | BigInt | evmone's secp256k1, with Montgomery field arithmetic on BigInt |
| SHA256, RIPEMD160, IDENTITY, BLAKE2F | None | Plain rv32 code |
| MODEXP | BigInt | Montgomery exponentiation for 256-bit operands; the generic path otherwise |
| ECADD, ECMUL, ECPAIRING | BigInt | bn254 field arithmetic |
| POINT_EVALUATION and the BLS12-381 precompiles | BigInt | blst, patched at build time to multiply on BigInt |
| P256VERIFY | BigInt | evmone's generic Montgomery field template |
| KECCAK256, and every hash the guest computes | keccak_f1600 | One delegation run per permutation |

The EVM's own 256-bit add, subtract and multiply, and its 32-byte copies, also run on BigInt.

## ZisK CSRs on PR #86

The ZisK guest exists only on [draft PR #86](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/pull/86). It calls ZisK's CSR precompiles, in the range `0x800` to `0x819`. Its `memcpy`, `memmove`, `memset` and `memcmp` go to ZisK's DMA precompiles.

| Area | ZisK precompiles |
|---|---|
| keccak-f | `0x800` |
| SHA256 | `0x805` |
| ADDMOD, MULMOD, and MODEXP up to 32-byte operands | `0x802` |
| ECRECOVER | `0x802`, `0x803`, `0x804`, plus square-root, inverse and GLV-split hints |
| ECADD, ECMUL, ECPAIRING | `0x802`, `0x806`, `0x807`, `0x808` to `0x80A` |
| BLS12-381 and KZG, through patched blst | `0x80B`, `0x80E` to `0x810`, plus an inverse hint |
| BLAKE2F | `0x819` |
| P256VERIFY | `0x802`, `0x817`, `0x818`, plus an inverse hint |
| Memory copy, set and compare | DMA `0x813`, `0x814`, `0x816` |
| EVM ADD, MUL, EXP, MOD | `0x811` for ADD, `0x801` for MUL and EXP, `0x802` for MOD |

RIPEMD160, IDENTITY and MODEXP with operands over 32 bytes stay in software. DIV, SDIV and SMOD use a division hint that the guest checks.

A hint, or fcall, returns a value the prover supplies freely. So the guest checks every hint before it uses the result. A bad inverse, square-root or division hint halts the run with an error, and no proof can exist. A bad GLV-split hint is the one exception. The guest then falls back to the software split, which needs no hint.

## Further reading

- [Execution pipeline](./execution-pipeline.md)
- [ZisK prover](../provers/zisk-prover.md)
- [`prover/guest_hypercube/src/include/sp1_syscalls.hpp`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/prover/guest_hypercube/src/include/sp1_syscalls.hpp): the SP1 ecall declarations
- [`docs/airbender_architecture.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/airbender_architecture.md): the Airbender guest, its memory map and CSR delegations

# Proof guarantees

Source: https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/inside-the-guest/proof-guarantees

_Each guest commits a fixed public-values layout, each host checks it to a different degree, and the verifying key ties a proof to one guest ELF._

# Proof guarantees

A proof says that one guest ELF ran on some input and committed some public values. The verifying key names the ELF. The public values say what the run found. What a consumer can trust depends on both, and on what the host checks.

## Public values per guest

### Hypercube MFBD guest, 112 bytes

The Hypercube MFBD guest commits 112 bytes. A release publishes it as `z6m_guest_hypercube_mfbd`.

| Offset | Bytes | Field | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 8 | `gas_used` | Gas used, little-endian. A failed run writes `UINT64_MAX` and a skipped run `UINT64_MAX - 1`. |
| 8 | 32 | `pre_state_root` | The parent state root the run starts from |
| 40 | 32 | `post_state_root` | The state root after the last block |
| 72 | 32 | `block_hash` | The hash of the last block |
| 104 | 8 | `chain_id` | The chain ID, little-endian |

The ZisK guest on draft PR #86 commits the same 112 bytes, in ZisK output slots 0 to 27.

### HashState guest, 43 bytes

On `statelessInputBytes` input, the HashState guest commits the SSZ `StatelessValidationResult`. This is the ERE guest, `stateless-validator-zilkworm-sp1-<SP1 version>`.

| Offset | Bytes | Field | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 32 | `new_payload_request_root` | The root of the block's `NewPayloadRequest` |
| 32 | 1 | `successful_validation` | 1 if the guest accepted the block, else 0 |
| 33 | 8 | `chain_id` | The chain ID, little-endian |
| 41 | 2 | `schema_id` | The input schema id, little-endian |

A rejected block still yields a result, with `successful_validation` set to 0. Only an input that does not decode gives the all-zero result. On EJSN input, the same guest writes the 112-byte layout above.

### Airbender guest, 32 bytes

The Airbender guest commits the hash of the last block it validated. It writes the hash's bytes in order, as little-endian words, to registers `a0` to `a7`. The hash binds the parent's state root and the block's post-state root, gas used and receipts root.

The value is zero when the run validated no block. That happens on an EJSN success, or on an MFBD whose every block is flagged expected-invalid. A failed or skipped run ends at `finish_error` and commits nothing, so it cannot be proven.

## Checks inside the guest

Before a DirectState guest commits, it checks the chain it ran:

- It takes the pre-state root from the parent header that the first block names.
- It requires each later block to extend the one before it.
- It checks each header's state root and gas used against the run.

An MFBD envelope can hold several bundles, each its own chain. The public values then cover the last validated block's bundle only.

The HashState guest checks that the witness headers chain by parent hash and end at the block's parent. Every account and storage read is checked against the parent state root. The guest rejects the block on a read it cannot confirm, or on a malformed witness. It accepts the block only if the folded post-state root matches the header.

## Checks in each host

The hosts check the public values to different degrees.

- The Airbender host derives the expected block hash from the input. It fails `execute`, `prove`, `verify`, `--test-service` and `--service` when the guest commits another.
- The Hypercube host parses the 112 bytes and logs them. It does not compare them with the input or with a node.
- The ERE harness, ere-hosts, compares the 43 bytes with the fixture's `statelessOutputBytes`. It records the result as `output_matched`.

A consumer that needs a Hypercube proof to match the chain compares `block_hash` and `post_state_root` with a node itself.

## Keys and guest builds

The verifying key is derived from the guest ELF, so a new guest build gets a new key. Each release publishes the key of each guest next to the guest. Build flags count too. The Hypercube MFBD guest is built with `USE_HASH_KEY=OFF` and the Airbender guest with `USE_HASH_KEY=ON`, and the key depends on that flag. The Airbender key also depends on the recursion verifier programs. Its prover accepts only their default `RECURSION_*_BLAKE` modes.

A zkVM update can rotate keys without any guest change. SP1 v6.9.0 loads a guest's initial memory differently from v6.6.0. SP1 keys published for alpha.6 therefore do not verify alpha.7 proofs. In the same release, a DirectState runner fix changed the MFBD and Airbender keys but not the ERE guest's key.

:::warning
Verify a proof with the key from the release that built its guest. Keys can change between releases even when the guest code does not.
:::

## Out of scope

A proof covers execution of the input it was given. It does not cover:

- Consensus validity. The proof does not say the block is canonical or attested.
- Blob availability. The guest never sees blob data, so the proof does not say the blobs were published.
- The parent header's origin. The guest anchors to the parent header in its input. A verifier checks the committed roots or block hash against a trusted node.

## Further reading

- [Execution pipeline](./execution-pipeline.md)
- [Witness formats](./witness-formats.md)
- [Releases and assets](../reference/releases-and-assets.md)
- [Ethproofs posting](../provers/ethproofs-posting.md)
- [`docs/architecture.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/architecture.md): the input envelope and the 112- and 32-byte layouts

# Execution spec tests

Source: https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/testing/execution-spec-tests

_Zilkworm runs the Ethereum execution spec tests natively and inside the Hypercube and Airbender guests, on a checksum-pinned fixture release._

# Execution spec tests

The Ethereum Execution Spec Tests, or EESTs, are the test vectors for the Ethereum execution layer. They are generated from the execution specs and cover every fork and many edge cases. A failing test usually points to a consensus bug. The fixtures ship as releases of [ethereum/execution-specs](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/releases), and the docs live at [eest.ethereum.org](https://eest.ethereum.org/). CI runs them natively and inside two zkVMs.

## Fixture pins

The fixtures come from release tarballs, pinned by checksum. The manifest `test-fixtures.json` names each tarball's URL, sha256, size and the paths to extract. It has one entry, `eest_stable`. That entry pins `tests@v21.0.1`, sha256 `b9b14391ed1a625e4ca9a058c055d0eacd98a42b76c7a6127c640cdc2d3c9439`, and extracts `fixtures/blockchain_tests`.

```bash
make test-fixtures
```

This runs `tools/test-fixtures.sh`. It downloads each tarball, checks its sha256 and extracts it into `test-fixtures-cache/<key>/`. A rerun does nothing while the pin matches. To move a pin, edit `test-fixtures.json`.

The HashState suite uses a second release, `tests-zkevm@v21.0.6`. The Makefile downloads it with `gh release download`, so it is not checksum-pinned.

## Native run

`make eest-blockchain-tests` needs CMake, Ninja, ctest, a C++23 compiler, Git, Python 3, curl and tar. It needs no Rust. Rust is needed only for the targets that build `z6m_prover`, such as `selftest` and `eest-prover-test`. [Building from source](../reference/building-from-source.md) lists the toolchain.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm
cd zilkworm
git submodule update --init --recursive
make eest-blockchain-tests
```

The target fetches the pinned tarball. It converts every JSON fixture to MFBD with `eest_to_flat_bundle bulk-convert`. The converted set lands in `test-fixtures-cache/mfbd-<sha>/`, named after the pin. A rerun skips the fetch and the conversion while the pin and the converter binary stay the same. The target then builds with `-DBUILD_TESTING=ON` and runs `ctest --parallel`, one case per fixture file.

## Make targets

| Target | What it does |
|---|---|
| `make test-fixtures` | Downloads, checks and extracts the pinned tarballs |
| `make selftest` | Converts one fixture, `add11`, to MFBD and runs it with `z6m_prover execute` |
| `make eest-blockchain-tests` | Runs the converted MFBD set through native ctest |
| `make eest-blockchain-tests-json` | Runs native ctest on the JSON fixtures, with no conversion |
| `make eest-prover-test` | Runs the MFBD set through `z6m_prover --test-service`, under the SP1 executor |
| `make eest-prover-test-json` | Runs the JSON fixtures through `z6m_prover --test-service` |
| `make eest-zkevm-tests` | Runs the `tests-zkevm@v21.0.6` fixtures through a native HashState build in `build/zkevm` |

`make tests` and `make tests-json` are broken: they pass `--execution-log-dir`, a flag `z6m_prover` does not have.

## Runs inside the zkVMs

CI also runs the pinned set inside the guests.

- The HyperCube EEST Blockchain Tests workflow builds `z6m_prover`. It runs the MFBD set through `tools/scripts/eest_runner.py` under the SP1 executor. The job fails above a set failure threshold.
- The Airbender EEST Blockchain Tests workflow builds the Airbender guest and host. It runs `make eest` in `prover/prover_airbender`. The job fails only on failures outside the known-failures lists.

The native suite runs in the EEST Blockchain Tests workflow. The QEMU runs are on [RISC-V tests under QEMU](./riscv-tests-under-qemu.md).

## Known failures

`zilk_core/dev/eest-known-failures.txt` lists fixtures that the runner gets wrong on every target. Their ctests are registered `WILL_FAIL`, so a listed fixture that passes again fails until it comes off the list. As of v0.1.0-alpha.7 the list holds only its header, so the native suite expects no failures.

`prover/prover_airbender/eest-known-failures.txt` lists 25 fixtures that the Airbender guest does not finish. They hit resource limits such as the execution cycle cap; they are not wrong results. The Airbender job adds the native list to its own.

## State-root check before a release

Before a release, `tools/scripts/release_state_root_check.sh` re-runs a directory of mainnet blocks natively. It builds `state_transition` in Release mode. It then runs every `<dir>/<N>/flatWitnessBundle<N>.mfbd` file in parallel. It reports each block whose output shows `ERROR: State Root Mismatch`, each timeout and each non-zero exit.

```bash
tools/scripts/release_state_root_check.sh --dir <blocks-dir> -j "$(nproc)"
```

`-s` and `-e` limit the block range. Logs go to `temp/release_state_root_check/` unless `-l` names another directory.

## Further reading

- [RISC-V tests under QEMU](./riscv-tests-under-qemu.md)
- [ERE validation](./ere-validation.md)
- [Building from source](../reference/building-from-source.md)
- [Benchmarks and CI](../reference/benchmarks-and-ci.md)
- [`test-fixtures.json`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/test-fixtures.json): the fixture pin

# RISC-V tests under QEMU

Source: https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/testing/riscv-tests-under-qemu

_The execution spec tests also run on bare-metal rv32im and rv64im builds of the core under QEMU, to catch bugs that only show on RISC-V._

# RISC-V tests under QEMU

A test should run as close to the real target as it can. For Zilkworm, the real target is a bare-metal RISC-V guest inside a zkVM. The QEMU runner in `qemu_runner/` builds the core for rv32im or rv64im. It then runs every [execution spec test](./execution-spec-tests.md) fixture on it under QEMU.

## Requirements

The QEMU suite uses the same pinned fixtures as the native suite, from `test-fixtures.json`. You need:

- CMake, Ninja, ctest, Git, Python 3, curl and tar
- a C++23 host compiler, for the fixture converter
- QEMU's RISC-V system emulators, `qemu-system-misc` on Ubuntu
- Node.js and npm, to install the cross-compiler

Install [xPack's RISC-V toolchain](https://xpack-dev-tools.github.io/riscv-none-elf-gcc-xpack/docs/install/). CI uses version 15.2.0-1.1:

```bash
npm i -g xpm
xpm install @xpack-dev-tools/riscv-none-elf-gcc@15.2.0-1.1 --global --verbose
export PATH=$HOME/.local/xPacks/@xpack-dev-tools/riscv-none-elf-gcc/15.2.0-1.1/.content/bin:$PATH
```

## Quickstart

Clone the repository and its submodule:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm
cd zilkworm
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

Run the suite on rv32im:

```bash
cd qemu_runner
make eest-rv32
```

The target fetches and converts the pinned fixtures, as the native suite does. It cross-compiles the core for rv32im and builds the test runner in `qemu_runner/build`. Then `ctest` starts one `qemu-system-riscv32` instance per fixture.

`make eest-rv64` runs the same suite on rv64im, in `qemu_runner/build64`. `make rerun-ctest` runs ctest again with verbose output and a longer per-test timeout. Add `ARCH=rv64` to target rv64im. The QEMU ctests read the native known-failures list, `zilk_core/dev/eest-known-failures.txt`.

## CI workflows

Two workflows run the suite: Qemu EESTs on RV32IM and Qemu EESTs on RV64IM. Each runs on pushes and pull requests to `main`, `master` and `release/*`. Each also runs on a cron every three days, and on demand. They use the `ghcr.io/erigontech/zilkworm-ci` image and add `qemu-system-misc`. Then they run `make xpack-elf-eest` and `make rerun-ctest`.

## Bugs that cross-architecture runs catch

The native suite catches logic and spec errors quickly. The QEMU runs catch bugs that stay hidden on a 64-bit x86 host. On rv32, `size_t`, `uintptr_t` and `long` are 32 bits wide, so truncation and overflow in size math show up. Alignment and struct-layout assumptions can break. `rv32im` has no atomics and no floating point, so an accidental use of either pulls in library code or breaks the link. A path that is cheap on x86_64 can also turn out costly in instructions on rv32, and in a zkVM every instruction is proven. The QEMU build is plain `rv32im`, so it does not check Airbender's ban on signed multiply and divide. The Airbender guest's post-link check covers that.

A test that fails on both native and QEMU usually has a logic or spec error. A test that fails only under QEMU points to a width, alignment or ISA issue.

## Further reading

- [Execution spec tests](./execution-spec-tests.md)
- [Execution pipeline](../inside-the-guest/execution-pipeline.md)
- [Benchmarks and CI](../reference/benchmarks-and-ci.md)
- [`qemu_runner/Makefile`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/qemu_runner/Makefile): the QEMU build and test targets

# ERE validation

Source: https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/testing/ere-validation

_The HashState guest runs in the ERE harness, which checks its output against each fixture and estimates its SP1 proving cost._

# ERE validation

The zkEVM benchmark workload, [eth-act/zkevm-benchmark-workload](https://github.com/eth-act/zkevm-benchmark-workload), runs stateless-validator guests inside zkVMs through ERE, [eth-act/ere](https://github.com/eth-act/ere). Its `ere-hosts` tool runs a guest on each fixture. Zilkworm takes part as an execution client, with its HashState guest on SP1.

## The ERE guest

The ERE guest is the HashState build of the Hypercube guest. `make z6m_guest_slib` builds it with `-DZ6M_HASH_STATE=ON`. It takes each fixture's `statelessInputBytes` unchanged, with no host adapter in between. [Witness formats](../inside-the-guest/witness-formats.md) describes that input.

Releases publish the guest as `stateless-validator-zilkworm-sp1-<version>.elf` and `.vk`. The name follows the ere-guests handbook pattern, `stateless-validator-<guest>-<zkVM>-<zkVM version>`. The version is the `sp1-sdk` tag that `derive_vk` builds against, read from `prover/stateless_validator/Cargo.toml`. For v0.1.0-alpha.7 the files are `stateless-validator-zilkworm-sp1-v6.9.0.elf` and `.vk`.

## Checks per fixture

For each fixture, ere-hosts feeds the guest the fixture's `statelessInputBytes`. The guest commits the 43-byte `StatelessValidationResult`. ere-hosts compares those bytes with the fixture's `statelessOutputBytes` and records `output_matched`. A cost run does not prove. It asks SP1 for an estimate of the proving cost instead. `tools/ere_compare.py` turns the per-fixture records into tables.

[Proof guarantees](../inside-the-guest/proof-guarantees.md) gives the 43-byte layout.

## Make targets

| Target | What it does |
|---|---|
| `make ere-bin` | Builds the HashState guest and derives its VK. Stages `build/ere-bin/stateless-validator-zilkworm-sp1.elf` and `.vk`. |
| `make ere-validate` | Runs every fixture in `ERE_INPUT_FOLDER` under ere-hosts, then checks `output_matched` with `ere_compare.py --validate` |
| `make ere-cost` | Runs ere-hosts with `--action estimate-cost`, then prints the cost table and report |
| `make ere-compare` | Runs `ere-cost`, then the same estimate for Reth's guest, and compares the two |
| `make ere-fixtures` | Generates EEST fixtures with `witness-generator-cli`; runs first only when `ERE_GEN_FIXTURES` is set |

The targets run `ere-hosts` inside a checkout of the benchmark workload, set by `ERE_WORKLOAD_DIR`. Every run passes `--force-rerun`, so no stale result from an older guest survives. `ERE_IMAGE_REGISTRY` points ERE at its prebuilt zkVM images on `ghcr.io/eth-act/ere`.

`ERE_BIN_PATH` names a local guest directory, such as `build/ere-bin`. When it is set, `ere-bin-link` links the files under the versioned name ere-hosts loads. It stops if the workload's SP1 version differs from the one `derive_vk` used. When `ERE_BIN_PATH` is empty, ere-hosts downloads the published guest.

## Local run

A local run needs Rust and a container engine, since ere-hosts drives ERE's SP1 server in a container. `tools/ere-fetch-fixtures.sh` fetches stateless fixtures from a public Sepolia block catalog. It caches them under `test-fixtures-cache/ere-sepolia/`. `latest N` extracts the N latest batches to `latest/`.

`ERE_WORKLOAD_DIR` must point at a workload checkout that has the `zilkworm` client. Today that is the `som/ere-v0.19.5` branch of the erigontech fork, which the first command clones. Run every command from the Zilkworm repository root.

```bash
git clone --branch som/ere-v0.19.5 https://github.com/erigontech/zkevm-benchmark-workload ../zkevm-benchmark-workload_fork
make ere-bin
tools/ere-fetch-fixtures.sh latest 1
make ere-validate \
    ERE_WORKLOAD_DIR=../zkevm-benchmark-workload_fork \
    ERE_BIN_PATH=build/ere-bin \
    ERE_INPUT_FOLDER=$(pwd)/test-fixtures-cache/ere-sepolia/latest
```

Swap `ere-validate` for `ere-cost` or `ere-compare` to estimate cost with the same variables.

## ERE benchmark workflow

`.github/workflows/ere-benchmark.yml` runs the same targets in CI. It runs on pushes to `release/*`, on demand, and when `release.yml` calls it after each `v*` release.

- Guest source. `build` runs `make ere-bin` at the run's ref. `release` downloads the release's ERE guest and checks it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
- Fixtures. The job fetches the latest batches of the public Sepolia catalog, one batch by default.
- Steps. It runs `ere-validate` and `ere-cost`, and `ere-compare` when the `compare` input is on.
- Repositories. It uses the erigontech forks of zkevm-benchmark-workload and ere-guests, branch `som/ere-v0.19.5`. The forks carry the Zilkworm client until it is upstreamed.
- Output. The step summary holds the result tables, and the run uploads the per-fixture records as the `ere-metrics` artifact.

`release.yml` calls the workflow with `compare: false`. Its comment says ere-guests had no Reth SP1 v6.9.0 guest yet. The alpha.7 release notes add that the fork registry has since taken one, so `make ere-compare` runs on the forks again.

## Results

[Releases and assets](../reference/releases-and-assets.md) lists the published ERE results with their release tags. Each workflow run's summary holds its own tables.

## Further reading

- [Releases and assets](../reference/releases-and-assets.md)

- [Execution spec tests](./execution-spec-tests.md)
- [`docs/ere_integration.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/ere_integration.md): harness setup, variables and past runs
- [`docs/hashstate.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/hashstate.md): the HashState backend
