# CLI reference

Source: https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/reference/cli-reference

_Look up the flags, subcommands, environment variables and exit codes of the three Zilkworm tools._

# CLI reference

Zilkworm has three command-line tools. `z6m_prover` drives the SP1 Hypercube guest. `z6m_prover_airbender` drives the Airbender guest. `state_transition` runs a block natively, outside any zkVM. The facts below match `v0.1.0-alpha.7`.

## z6m_prover (Hypercube)

The release ships this binary as `z6m_prover_hypercube`. `make z6m_prover` builds it at `prover/target/release/z6m_prover`. It has three forms:

```bash
z6m_prover --service [flags]         # fetch, execute and prove in a loop
z6m_prover --test-service [flags]    # execute downloaded blocks or EEST fixtures offline
z6m_prover <subcommand> [flags]      # fetch, execute, prove, setup or verify once
```

With no mode and no subcommand it exits with an error. It loads a `.env` file from the working directory at startup.

### Top-level flags

| Flag | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `--service` | off | Run the service loop. Needs `--rpc-url`. |
| `--test-service` | off | Execute on the CPU, with no RPC and no proving. With `--test-dir` it runs EEST fixtures. Otherwise it runs bundles from `--data-dir` between `--start-block` and `--end-block`. Conflicts with `--service` and with any subcommand. |
| `--rpc-url` | none | JSON-RPC endpoint. It must serve `debug_getRawBlock` and `debug_executionWitness`. |
| `--data-dir` | `temp` | Root data directory. Blocks go to `<data-dir>/blocks/<N>/`, logs to the root. |
| `--save-all-responses` | off | Also save the raw RPC JSON next to each bundle. In service mode it also fetches blocks that match no interval. |
| `--download-only` | off | Service mode: fetch bundles only. It overrides `--prove-every` and `--execute-every`. |
| `--prove-every` | unset | Service mode: prove blocks whose number is a multiple of N. 0 or unset means never. |
| `--execute-every` | unset | Execute blocks whose number is a multiple of N, unless they are proved. `--test-service` without `--test-dir` defaults it to 1 and rejects 0. |
| `--post-every` | unset | Unused. |
| `--start-block` | chain head + 1 | First block. `--test-service` needs it unless `--test-dir` is set. |
| `--end-block` | follow the head | Last block, inclusive. The service exits after it. |
| `--execution-log-file` | `executionLogs.log` in the data or test directory | Read by `--test-service` only. The service and `execute` always append to `<data-dir>/executionLogs.log`. |
| `--test-dir` | none | EEST fixtures for `--test-service`, scanned recursively for `.mfbd` and `.json` files. |
| `--max-file-size` | `20971520` | `--test-service --test-dir` skips larger files. 0 means no limit. |
| `--pk-path` | `pk.bin` | Unused. The proving key is generated in-process. |
| `--proof-type` | `compressed` | Service-mode proof mode: `core`, `compressed`, `groth16` or `plonk`. Unknown values fall back to `compressed`. |
| `--ethproofs-endpoint`, `--ethproofs-token`, `--ethproofs-cluster-id` | none | Ethproofs reporting in `--service`. Set all three, or reporting stays off without a warning. |

### Subcommands

| Subcommand | Options | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `fetch` | `--rpc-url`, `--block-number`, `--data-dir`, `--save-all-responses`, `--geth` | Fetch one block and its witness and write `<data-dir>/blocks/<N>/flatWitnessBundle<N>.mfbd`. An unset or 0 block number means the chain head. A bundle already on disk is reused. |
| `execute` | `--block-number`, `--file-name`, `--is-test`, `--data-dir` | Run the guest on the CPU executor without proving. |
| `prove` | as `execute`, plus `--pk-path`, `--proof-path`, `--proof-type` | Prove one block. The three extra options are unused. See the limits below. |
| `setup` | `--pk-path`, `--vk-path` | No-op. Nothing is written. |
| `verify` | `--proof-path`, `--vk-path` | No-op. No verification runs. |

`execute` and `prove` read `<data-dir>/blocks/<N>/flatWitnessBundle<N>.mfbd`. With `--is-test` they read `ethTests<N>.json` as an EEST fixture. `--file-name` overrides the block-number lookup.

`execute` prints `Executed block <N> (gas_used=..., cycles=..., prover_gas=..., syscall_count=...)`. It appends a line to `<data-dir>/executionLogs.log`. It exits 1 when `gas_used` is 0.

`--geth` exists only on `fetch`. The service always reads the reth and alloy witness shape.

Limits of `prove` as of `v0.1.0-alpha.7`:

- It always uses the CUDA prover in compressed mode. It ignores `SP1_PROVER` and `--proof-type`.
- It discards the proof. Nothing is written to disk, and the summary line prints `gas_used=0` and an empty path.
- A key setup failure prints `ERROR` and still exits 0. A proving failure is not reported.
- It never posts to Ethproofs.

Use `--service` to get proof files.

### Environment variables

- `SP1_PROVER` selects the service-mode backend. Only `cuda` is special-cased, as the local GPU prover. Any other value, or none, gives the CPU prover. `execute` always uses the CPU, and `prove` always uses CUDA.
- `NETWORK_PRIVATE_KEY` is listed in `.env.example` for the Succinct Prover Network. It is unused, because `network` and `mock` modes are not wired up.
- `RUST_LOG` sets the log filter. It defaults to `warn`.

The Ethproofs settings are flags only. This binary reads no `ETHPROOFS_*` variables.

## z6m_prover_airbender

`make z6m_prover_airbender` builds it at `prover/prover_airbender/target/release/z6m_prover_airbender`. The image `ghcr.io/erigontech/zilkworm-airbender` ships it with the guest. It runs as `--service`, as `--test-service`, or with one subcommand.

### Top-level flags

| Flag | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `--service` | off | Run the proving service. Needs `--rpc-url`. Conflicts with subcommands. |
| `--test-service` | off | Execute downloaded blocks from `--start-block` to `--end-block` on the simulator. Needs both. Conflicts with subcommands. |
| `--data-dir` | `temp` | Root directory with a `blocks/` subdirectory. |
| `--start-block`, `--end-block` | unset | Block range. |
| `--execution-log-file` | `<data-dir>/executionLogs.log` | Read by `--test-service` only. |
| `--guest-bin` | `prover/guest_airbender/build/z6m_guest` | Guest path without the `.bin` or `.text` extension. The default needs the repo root as working directory. |
| `--cycles` | `5000000000` | Simulator cycle bound. Proving clamps it to `1073741822`. |
| `--replay-threads` | unset, 8 on the GPU backend | CPU threads that replay the trace while proving. Env `Z6M_REPLAY_THREADS`. Also accepted after a subcommand. |
| `--rpc-url` | none | JSON-RPC endpoint. Required for `--service`. |
| `--ws-url` | none | WebSocket endpoint for `newHeads`. Without it the service polls `--rpc-url`. |
| `--gpu` | off | Prove on the GPU in service mode. Required with `--prove-every`. |
| `--prove-every` | unset | Service mode: prove blocks whose number is a multiple of N. |
| `--execute-every` | unset | Service mode: execute without proving every N-th block. |
| `--post-every` | unset | Accepted and never read. |
| `--output-dir` | `proofs` | Service proofs go to `<output-dir>/<N>/proof.bin`. |
| `--save-all-responses` | off | Save the raw RPC responses. |
| `--fetch-timeout` | `60` | Seconds one fetch attempt may take. Minimum 1. |
| `--max-lag` | `10` | Blocks the service may fall behind the tip before it skips ahead. 0 never skips. |
| `--ethproofs-endpoint`, `--ethproofs-token`, `--ethproofs-cluster-id` | none | Ethproofs reporting. Env `ETHPROOFS_ENDPOINT`, `ETHPROOFS_TOKEN`, `ETHPROOFS_CLUSTER_ID`. Set all three or nothing is posted. |

### Subcommands

| Subcommand | Options | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `execute` | `--block-number`, `--file-name`, `--data-dir`, `--is-test`, `--flamegraph <svg>` | Run the guest on the simulator. Check the committed block hash against the input. Fail if the guest does not finish successfully. |
| `vk` | `--output`, default `vk.bin` | Compute the guest's EVKEY001 v2 verification key from the guest and the `FSV_DIR` programs. |
| `prove` | `--block-number`, `--file-name`, `--data-dir`, `--is-test`, `--backend gpu` or `cpu`, `--output-dir` | Run a simulator preflight, prove to the final recursion layer, check the output and write `<output-dir>/proof.bin`. Defaults: `gpu`, `proofs`. |
| `bench` | `--file-name` (required), `--iterations` (default 5), `--backend` | Prove one MFBD file repeatedly with one prover. Print each time and the min, median and max. |
| `verify` | `--proof`, `--vk`, and `--file-name` or `--block-hash` | Verify the proof against the key. Check that its output is the hash of the input's last valid block, or the given hash. |

Without `--file-name`, input comes from `<data-dir>/blocks/<N>/flatWitnessBundle<N>.mfbd`. If that file is missing, the legacy `unifiedBlockAndStateRlp<N>.bin` is tried. With `--is-test` the input is an EEST JSON fixture. Proof files are gzip EPROOF01 v2. The `cpu` backend is slow; [Airbender prover](../provers/airbender-prover.md) gives its memory need.

`execute` and `--test-service` append to the execution log. `execute` warns when a run has more cycles than the prover takes.

### Environment variables

| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `Z6M_REPLAY_THREADS` | Same as `--replay-threads`. |
| `FSV_DIR` | Directory of the `fsv_*` recursion verifier programs. Unset, the prover uses `tools/gkr_verifier` of the zksync-airbender checkout it was built from. The image sets it. |
| `RISCV_MERGE_WINDOW` | Leave unset. The binary sets it to 0, and any other value is an error. The prover's JIT would otherwise fuse word stores the guest jumps into, and prove a wrong run. |
| `Z6M_CONCURRENT_PREFLIGHT` | When set, the service simulates each block alongside proving instead of first. A block the guest rejects then stops the service. |
| `RECURSION_UNROLLED_BLAKE`, `RECURSION_BRIDGE_BLAKE`, `RECURSION_FINAL_BLAKE`, `RECURSION_UNIFIED_BLAKE` | Leave unset. Other values make proofs no published key accepts, so `prove` and `bench` refuse to start. |
| `ETHPROOFS_ENDPOINT`, `ETHPROOFS_TOKEN`, `ETHPROOFS_CLUSTER_ID` | Same as the Ethproofs flags. |
| `RUST_LOG` | Log filter. Defaults to `info`. |

### Docker entrypoint

The image's entrypoint runs the prover with any arguments you pass, plus `--guest-bin`. With no arguments it runs the service from the environment. It first computes the verification key into `$DATA_DIR/vk-<rev>-<id>/vk.bin`. Then it runs `--service --gpu` and restarts the service whenever it exits. Proofs go to `$DATA_DIR/proofs/<N>/proof.bin`.

| Variable | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `RPC_URL` | required | JSON-RPC endpoint that serves `debug_executionWitness`. |
| `WS_URL` | none | WebSocket endpoint for `newHeads`. Without it the service polls. |
| `PROVE_EVERY` | `100` | Prove blocks whose number is a multiple of this. |
| `EXECUTE_EVERY` | none | Execute without proving every N-th block. |
| `START_BLOCK` | chain tip | First block. A restart drops it and starts at the tip. |
| `FETCH_TIMEOUT` | `60` | Seconds one fetch attempt may take. |
| `MAX_LAG` | `10` | Blocks behind the tip before the service skips ahead. 0 never skips. |
| `DATA_DIR` | `/data` | Key, blocks, logs and proofs. Mount a volume here. |
| `ETHPROOFS_ENDPOINT`, `ETHPROOFS_TOKEN`, `ETHPROOFS_CLUSTER_ID` | none | Post to Ethproofs. With any one unset the run is a dry run. |
| `RESTART_DELAY` | `30` | Seconds to wait before a restart. |
| `PROVER_EXTRA_ARGS` | none | More prover options, split on spaces. |

## state_transition

`state_transition` runs the whole state transition natively. The release ships it as `state_transition_linux_x86_64`. A local build puts it at `build/zilk_core/dev/cli/state_transition`.

```bash
state_transition <flatWitnessBundle.mfbd>|<test.json>|<test_dir>
```

A path ending in `.json` runs as an EEST blockchain test. Any other file runs as an MFBD bundle. A directory is scanned recursively. For a bundle it prints `Cumulative Gas Used: <n>`, `FAIL: <path>` or `SKIP: <path>`.

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Passed. For a directory: at least one file passed and none failed. |
| 1 | Failed, or no argument given. For a directory: any file failed. |
| 2 | Skipped. For a directory: nothing passed. |
| 3 | The bundle could not be read, or an exception was thrown. |
| 4 | An unknown exception. |

Directory mode only picks up `.json` and `.bin` files, so a directory of `.mfbd` files runs nothing and exits 2. Pass bundles one at a time instead.

# Releases and assets

Source: https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/reference/releases-and-assets

_Each Zilkworm release ships host binaries, guest images and verification keys, listed here with its measured results._

# Releases and assets

Releases are on the [GitHub releases page](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/releases). All of them are pre-releases so far. Each release body opens with the matching section of `CHANGELOG.md`.

Performance numbers on this site appear only here. Each one comes from the CHANGELOG section of the tag on its line.

## Current status

- Latest release: `v0.1.0-alpha.7`, published 25 October 2026.
- EEST pin: `tests@v21.0.1`.
- Ethproofs: Airbender live. The `v0.1.0-alpha.5` result below has Ethproofs provenance. There is no Hypercube cluster on Ethproofs.

The overview's status strip reads `src/data/status.json` in the docs repository. Update that file and this page together on each release.

## Release history

| Tag | Title | Highlights |
|---|---|---|
| `v0.1.0-alpha.1` | First Public Alpha | The C++ guest on SP1 Hypercube, with precompiles on SP1 syscalls. |
| `v0.1.0-alpha.2` | More performance more testing and more stability | "Close to 10% improved proving time". The EEST suite runs inside the Hypercube prover. |
| `v0.1.0-alpha.2-ere` | ERE zkEVM benchmark integration | alpha.2 plus the ERE benchmark integration. It has no CHANGELOG section. |
| `v0.1.0-alpha.3` | MFBD witness format, pre-trie validation and Amsterdam | The MFBD bundle, and pre-state checks against the parent root. |
| `v0.1.0-alpha.4` | ERE stateless input, stateless new-payload checks and Sepolia | 33,635 of 33,637 `output_matched` on tests-zkevm v21.0.1. Estimated prover cost 0.500x Reth 0.1.0-rc.4's on Sepolia. |
| `v0.1.0-alpha.5` | Real-time proving with Airbender v3 | Airbender proves 200 consecutive mainnet blocks at a 3.4 s median on 2x RTX 5090, slowest 6.1 s. Ethproofs provenance, 15 October 2026. 2.58 s median on 4x RTX 5090. |
| `v0.1.0-alpha.6` | Native statelessInputBytes with the HashState backend | CI 200-block benchmark: Hypercube guest cycles from 23.21B at alpha.5 to 17.44B (-24.9%), Airbender from 27.86B to 27.65B (-0.8%). The HashState ERE guest is at Z/R 0.477 against Reth 0.1.0-rc.4. |
| `v0.1.0-alpha.7` | SP1 v6.9.0 and a leaner HashState guest | ERE estimated cost −1.70% on Sepolia 11982400..11982499. The SP1 bump leaves guest cycles as on alpha.6. |

## Assets in v0.1.0-alpha.7

| Asset | What it is | zkVM | Input |
|---|---|---|---|
| `z6m_prover_hypercube` | The Hypercube host `z6m_prover` for x86_64 Linux, with the MFBD guest embedded | SP1 Hypercube v6.9.0 | `.mfbd`, or EEST JSON with `--is-test` |
| `z6m_guest_hypercube_mfbd.elf` | DirectState guest, rv64im, built `USE_HASH_KEY=OFF` | SP1 | MFBD, EJSN |
| `z6m_guest_hypercube_mfbd.vk` | Its SP1 verifying key, from `derive_vk` | SP1 | none |
| `stateless-validator-zilkworm-sp1-v6.9.0.elf` | HashState guest, rv64im; the ERE guest | SP1 v6.9.0 | Raw `statelessInputBytes`, EJSN |
| `stateless-validator-zilkworm-sp1-v6.9.0.vk` | Its SP1 verifying key, named as the ere-guests handbook asks | SP1 | none |
| `state_transition_linux_x86_64` | Native runner, DirectState | none | `.mfbd`, `.json` or a directory |
| `z6m_guest_airbender.bin` | rv32 guest image, copied out of the release image, built `USE_HASH_KEY=ON` | Airbender v3 | MFBD, EJSN |
| `z6m_guest_airbender.text` | Text section of the same guest | Airbender v3 | none |
| `z6m_guest_airbender.vk` | EVKEY001 v2 verification key, computed on CPU by the image's prover | Airbender v3 | none |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt` | sha256 of every file above | none | none |

The release also tags the image `ghcr.io/erigontech/zilkworm-airbender:<tag>`. Its notes give the image digest and the sha256 of `z6m_guest_airbender.vk`. Upload that key to your Ethproofs cluster so its proofs show as verified.

## Verification keys

A key belongs to one guest build. The Hypercube MFBD guest is built with `USE_HASH_KEY=OFF`, and the Airbender guest with `USE_HASH_KEY=ON`. The key depends on that flag, so a local build reproduces a published key only with the same setting.

Keys also change when the guest code does not. Keys published for `v0.1.0-alpha.6` do not verify `v0.1.0-alpha.7` proofs. SP1 v6.9.0 loads a guest's initial memory correctly, where v6.6.0 zeroed up to four bytes of it ([sp1#2981](https://github.com/succinctlabs/sp1/pull/2981)). In `v0.1.0-alpha.7` the MFBD and Airbender guests and their keys also changed with [#141](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/pull/141). Always check a proof against the key from its own release.

## Older asset names

- `v0.1.0-alpha.5` shipped the Hypercube guest as `z6m_guest_hypercube.{elf,vk}`.
- `v0.1.0-alpha.6` release notes call the ERE guest `z6m_guest_hypercube_slib`. Its assets are `stateless-validator-zilkworm-sp1-v6.6.0.{elf,vk}`.

## Release procedure

1. Create a branch, usually `release/X.Y.Z`.
2. Bump `PROJECT_VERSION` in `CMakeLists.txt` to `X.Y.Z`.
3. Add a `## vX.Y.Z - <title>` section to `CHANGELOG.md`. It becomes the release body.
4. Commit and push the branch.
5. Tag the release commit `vX.Y.Z` and push the tag. The tag must equal `PROJECT_VERSION`, or the workflow fails.

The `Release` workflow then tags the Airbender image, builds the assets, writes `SHA256SUMS.txt` and publishes the release. It ends with an ERE benchmark run on the published guest. Tag a commit on `main` only after its `Airbender Prover Image` run has finished. Otherwise the image is built twice, and its commit and release tags can name two different builds.

- [Choosing a prover](../provers/choosing-a-prover.md)

- [`docs/release.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/release.md)
- [`CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

# Building from source

Source: https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/reference/building-from-source

_Build the native tools, the guests and the host provers from source, and run the unit tests._

# Building from source

## Native build

You need CMake 3.28 or newer, Ninja and GCC 15. Clone the repository with its one submodule, `third_party/evmone`. It holds ZVM1, the Zilkworm fork of evmone.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm
cd zilkworm
git submodule update --init --recursive
cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -B build -G Ninja -S .
cmake --build build -j$(nproc)
```

The guests also need the xPack `riscv-none-elf-gcc` cross-compiler. CI pins version `15.2.0-1.1`:

```bash
npm install -g xpm
xpm install @xpack-dev-tools/riscv-none-elf-gcc@15.2.0-1.1 --global
```

The Makefile puts the first xPack GCC it finds under `~/.local/xPacks` on `PATH`. On macOS it looks under `~/Library/xPacks`. Keep only `15.2.0-1.1` installed, or a guest can build with an older compiler.

## state_transition

The native build produces `build/zilk_core/dev/cli/state_transition`. It runs the whole state transition outside any zkVM.

```bash
build/zilk_core/dev/cli/state_transition <flatWitnessBundle.mfbd>
```

It also takes an EEST blockchain-test JSON or a directory. [CLI reference](./cli-reference.md#state_transition) lists its inputs and exit codes.

## Converters

Three converters sit next to it. Each writes the MFBD bundle that [Witness formats](../inside-the-guest/witness-formats.md) describes.

- `json_witness_to_flat_bundle` reads a witness JSON document on stdin and writes the bundle to stdout.
- `legacy_to_flat_bundle <in.bin> <out.mfbd>` converts an older `unifiedBlockAndStateRlp<N>.bin` file.
- `eest_to_flat_bundle` converts EEST blockchain-test JSON. `emit --json <PATH> --index <N>` writes one case to stdout. `bulk-convert --input-dir <D> --output-dir <D>` mirrors a whole tree.

## Guest targets

Each guest target cross-compiles the C++ core for one zkVM.

| Target | Builds | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `make z6m_guest` | Hypercube DirectState guest for MFBD input, `USE_HASH_KEY=OFF` | `prover/guest_hypercube/build/z6m_guest.elf` |
| `make z6m_guest_slib` | Hypercube HashState guest for `statelessInputBytes`, with `-DZ6M_HASH_STATE=ON` | `prover/guest_hypercube/build-slib/z6m_guest.elf` |
| `make z6m_guest_airbender` | Airbender guest, `USE_HASH_KEY=ON` | `prover/guest_airbender/build/z6m_guest.bin` and `.text` |
| `make z6m_guest_zisk` | ZisK guest, only on PR #86; see [ZisK prover](../provers/zisk-prover.md) | `prover/guest_zisk/build/z6m_guest.elf` |

The Hypercube guests use the toolchain file `prover/guest_hypercube/cmake/riscv64im-sp1.cmake`. The Airbender guest uses `prover/guest_airbender/cmake/riscv32im.cmake`. `USE_HASH_KEY` changes the verification key, as [Releases and assets](./releases-and-assets.md#verification-keys) explains.

## Host targets

| Target | Builds | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `make z6m_prover` | The MFBD guest and the Hypercube host that embeds it | `prover/target/release/z6m_prover` |
| `make z6m_prover_slib` | The same host with the HashState guest embedded | `prover/target/release/z6m_prover` |
| `make z6m_prover_airbender` | The Airbender guest and its host | `prover/prover_airbender/target/release/z6m_prover_airbender` |
| `make derive_vk` | `derive_vk <elf> <vk>`, which writes a guest's 32-byte SP1 key | `prover/target/release/derive_vk` |

`make z6m_prover` and `make z6m_prover_slib` write the same binary, so the last one built wins. `make z6m_guest_vk` and `make ere-bin` run `derive_vk` with `SP1_PROVER=mock`.

:::caution
A tree that ran `make z6m_prover_slib` before `v0.1.0-alpha.7` must delete `prover/guest_hypercube/build/z6m_guest.elf` once. Otherwise `make z6m_prover` keeps embedding the HashState guest.
:::

The Airbender host builds with GPU support by default. Without CUDA, build it with `cargo build --release --no-default-features` in `prover/prover_airbender`, as CI does. Each Rust workspace pins its toolchain in `rust-toolchain.toml`.

## Tests

The unit tests build and run as in CI:

```bash
cmake -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DBUILD_TESTING=ON
cmake --build build --target zilkworm.tests
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure --parallel
```

Add `-DZ6M_HASH_STATE=ON` to run them on the HashState backend. The EEST suites are on [Execution spec tests](../testing/execution-spec-tests.md) and [RISC-V tests under QEMU](../testing/riscv-tests-under-qemu.md).

## Code style

The C++ code follows Silkworm's style: the C++ Core Guidelines and Google's C++ style guide, with project changes.
`zilk_core/.clang-format` holds the format rules.
`zilk_core/.clang-tidy` holds the lint checks.

## Repo docs

- [`docs/architecture.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/architecture.md): the layers, the input envelope and the public values.
- [`docs/mfbd_design_specs.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/mfbd_design_specs.md): the MFBD spec for producers and verifiers.
- [`docs/hashstate.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/hashstate.md): the HashState backend and its SSZ input.
- [`docs/airbender_architecture.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/airbender_architecture.md): the rv32 guest, its toolchain and its CSR delegations.
- [`docs/release.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/release.md): the release process.

# Benchmarks and CI

Source: https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/reference/benchmarks-and-ci

_Make targets benchmark the Hypercube, HashState, Airbender and ERE paths, and GitHub workflows run them._

# Benchmarks and CI

The benchmarks below measure cycles and estimated prover cost. Their results for each release are on [Releases and assets](./releases-and-assets.md).

## Hypercube 200-block benchmark

`make sp1-benchmark` runs the Hypercube MFBD guest over 200 mainnet blocks. It builds `z6m_prover`, then runs `make sp1-benchmark-corpus`, then `tools/scripts/sp1_benchmark.py`.

`sp1-benchmark-corpus` converts each `temp/200_benchmark_blocks/<N>/unifiedBlockAndStateRlp<N>.bin` with `legacy_to_flat_bundle`. The bundles go to `temp/200_benchmark_blocks_mfbd_v2/<N>/`. `BENCH_SRC_DIR` and `BENCH_CORPUS_DIR` override the two paths. CI downloads the raw blocks from the [`benchmark-200-spread`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm-testdata/releases/tag/benchmark-200-spread) release of `erigontech/zilkworm-testdata`.

The script takes `--dir`, and optionally `--start` and `--count`. It writes `execution.log` and `summary.md` to `temp/benchmarks/benchmark_<timestamp>/`. It does not compare against a baseline. To compare two builds, run it on each and compare the totals.

## HashState benchmark

`make slib-benchmark` measures the SP1 cycles of the HashState guest. It downloads the 30M-gas `tests-zkevm-benchmark@v21.0.5` fixtures with `gh release download`, so `gh` must be logged in. It builds `z6m_prover_slib` and runs each case through `z6m_prover execute --is-test`. Per-case results go to `temp/slib_benchmark/per_case.csv`.

These numbers are not the production path. `execute --is-test` sends the whole fixture JSON to the guest, and parsing it is about half the cycles. The ERE benchmark below measures the production input. [`docs/slib_benchmark.md`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/blob/main/docs/slib_benchmark.md) has the details.

`z6m_prover_slib` replaces `prover/target/release/z6m_prover`. Run `make z6m_prover` again before an MFBD run.

## Airbender benchmark

`tools/scripts/airbender_benchmark.sh --dir <corpus>` runs `z6m_prover_airbender execute` on every bundle in the corpus. It takes the layout that `make sp1-benchmark-corpus` writes. It reports gas and cycle statistics, with logs in `temp/airbender_benchmark/`. Options `-j`, `-s`, `-e`, `-l` and `-t` set the jobs, block range, log directory and per-block timeout.

The prover's `bench` subcommand is different. It proves one block several times.

## ERE benchmark

The ERE benchmark runs the HashState guest inside SP1 through `ere-hosts`, on each fixture's `statelessInputBytes`. `make ere-cost` estimates the guest's SP1 cost and prints a cost table. `make ere-compare` runs `ere-cost`, then estimates Reth's cost on the same fixtures and compares the two. `make ere-compare -o ere-cost` reuses an earlier `ere-cost` run.

Both targets run in a `zkevm-benchmark-workload` checkout at `ERE_WORKLOAD_DIR`. Set `ERE_BIN_PATH=build/ere-bin` to run the guest from `make ere-bin`. Without it, the published guest is downloaded. [ERE validation](../testing/ere-validation.md) covers the setup, `ere-validate` and the `output_matched` check.

## CI workflows

All workflows live in [`.github/workflows/`](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/tree/main/.github/workflows). Most run in the `ghcr.io/erigontech/zilkworm-ci` image.

| File | Name | What it runs | Trigger |
|---|---|---|---|
| `unit-tests.yml` | Unit Tests | `zilkworm.tests` three ways: Debug, HashState, and rv32 paths with ASan and UBSan | push, PR to main, master; dispatch |
| `eest-blockchain-tests.yml` | EEST Blockchain Tests | `make eest-blockchain-tests`, native on MFBD | push, PR to main, master, release/*; dispatch |
| `hypercube-eest.yml` | HyperCube EEST Blockchain Tests | `make z6m_prover`, then `eest_runner.py` over the MFBD corpus on the SP1 executor | push, PR to main, master, release/* on path changes; dispatch |
| `sp1-benchmark.yml` | Hypercube 200-block Bench | `sp1-benchmark-corpus` and `sp1_benchmark.py` | push, PR to main, master, release/*; dispatch |
| `hypercube-slib-benchmark.yml` | HyperCube slib Benchmark | `make slib-benchmark` | dispatch only |
| `airbender-eest.yml` | Airbender EEST Blockchain Tests | The guest, the host without GPU features, and `make eest` in `prover/prover_airbender` | push, PR to main, master on path changes; dispatch |
| `airbender-benchmark.yml` | Airbender 200-block Bench | `airbender_benchmark.sh` on the 200-block corpus | push, PR to main, master; dispatch |
| `airbender-image.yml` | Airbender Prover Image | Build and push `ghcr.io/erigontech/zilkworm-airbender`; Airbender release assets | push to main on path changes, PR on path changes; dispatch; called by Release |
| `qemu-eest-blockchain.yml` | Qemu EESTs on RV32IM | `qemu_runner` targets `xpack-elf-eest` and `rerun-ctest` | push, PR to main, master, release/*; every 3 days; dispatch |
| `qemu-eest-blockchain-rv64.yml` | Qemu EESTs on RV64IM | The same with `ARCH=rv64` | push, PR to main, master, release/*; every 3 days; dispatch |
| `ere-benchmark.yml` | ERE Benchmark | `ere-bin`, `ere-validate`, `ere-cost`, and `ere-compare` when asked | push to release/*; dispatch; called by Release |
| `release.yml` | Release | Tag check, Airbender image, `make z6m_prover z6m_guest_vk ere-bin`, `state_transition`, `release-artifacts`, publish, then an ERE run without Reth | tag `v*`; dispatch |
| `ci-image.yml` | Build CI Image | Build `ghcr.io/erigontech/zilkworm-ci` | push to main, master, release/* on Dockerfile changes; dispatch |
| `zisk-eest.yml` | ZisK EEST Blockchain Tests | PR #86 only. EEST under `ziskemu`, execute only | push, PR to main, master, release/* on path changes; dispatch |
| `zisk-benchmark.yml` | ZisK 200-block Bench | PR #86 only. The 200-block corpus under `ziskemu`, execute only | push, PR to main, master, release/* on path changes; dispatch |

The two ZisK workflows exist only on [PR #86](https://github.com/erigontech/zilkworm/pull/86). They run in `ghcr.io/erigontech/zilkworm-ci-zisk`.
